affordance_in_statement: You are guaranteed that m = n - 1, and that the full set of m proposed transpositions generates the entire symmetric group S_n.
removal_suggestion: No task-preserving removal is available. The generation guarantee makes the transposition graph connected, and m = n - 1 therefore makes it a tree; connecting the target orbits is intrinsically the minimum weighted Steiner subtree problem on that tree. Defeating this reduction would require changing the structural premise or the task.

common_affordance: The guaranteed connected transposition graph has n vertices and n - 1 edges, so it is a tree and the orbit requirement reduces to the unique weighted subtree connecting the targets.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It applies a generic Kruskal/DSU approach to connect the required vertices instead of exploiting the unique tree paths and computing the terminal Steiner subtree; its handling of non-target vertices can therefore select the wrong edge set or cost.
It sorts all edges and runs a general MST-style union process, treating the problem as ordinary MST construction rather than retaining exactly the edges on paths between targets.

recommended_edit: None that preserves the stated task and immutable constraints. Any edit that defeats both surviving solutions must remove or alter the connected n-1-edge structural guarantee, which changes the problem rather than merely re-presenting it.
